_note: SUBSCRIPTION INVENTORY — the ONE file a new user edits to port this system. It describes what you pay for and which providers each plan backs. Nothing here is invariant policy; it is your account reality. Change a plan → edit only this file (and usage-windows.json anchors). `grants.fable` is authoritative for Fable availability and is re-checked by bin/detect-capability.py so a silent downgrade is caught. Seats are real accounts; teamclaude rotates across the Claude seats. To hand this to a different user: replace these entries with theirs, run `bin/doctor.py`, and the whole system re-routes with no prose edits.

codex-200.notes: One Codex plan backs Terra, Luna, and Sol. Any may be the requested per-run dispatcher when qualified; Terra/Luna share codex-plan usage while Sol has a separate tracked role row.

grok-heavy.notes: Abundant Grok CLI volume. All three standing named-agent normal routes are hard-parked until their shared code-owned input bindings exist; observed browser/Clarity/deposit capability, profile sync, and role tests are additional gates. Transport-only smoke remains available. Set the weekly anchor in usage-windows.json when known.

cursor-ultra.notes: First-party Cursor Models pool (drain first for IDE work) + Other Models $400/mo (Last $). Cursor Sol is NOT Codex Sol; different meter.

claude-max-200.notes: Highest-capacity Claude seat. Carries Fable + Opus 5. Prefer this seat for Fable-required frontier review.

claude-team-125-a.notes: Team premium seat with Fable. Confirm the Fable grant with bin/detect-capability.py — Team STANDARD does not include Fable.

claude-team-125-b.notes: Second Team premium seat with Fable.

claude-pro-25-a.notes: Pro seat — extends Opus 5 capacity; NO Fable. Used to preserve the higher seats for Fable-required work.

claude-pro-25-b.notes: Second Pro seat — Opus 5 capacity only.

derived_note: Fable-capable Claude seats: any subscription with grants.fable == true (currently Max + 2 Team = 3 seats). Opus-capable seats: grants.opus == true (all 5). resolve-route.py treats Fable as available only if at least one Fable-capable seat is live per usage-status AND detect-capability has not recorded a downgrade. Fable stays OUT of the gating order (rare architecture/long-horizon escalation, same family as Opus). The live review order is Opus 5 → Codex Sol → Review E (if wired), filtered to live_verified routes — Fable absence never changes that order.

portability_examples.no-codex-user: Removing Codex removes Sol/Terra/Luna dispatch candidates, the OpenAI review family, and Terra MCP volume. Update entrypoint profiles/fallbacks; doctor.py must pass.
portability_examples.solo-pro-user: A single Claude Pro user keeps only claude-pro-25-a (rename freely), grants.fable:false; the review order collapses to opus-5 → review-e (if wired) → stop; Grok/Cursor entries removed.
